commits.message:
feat(frontend): add pagination to every high-volume review page

Skills taxonomy, job titles taxonomy, the parsed-email drafts list, and
the taxonomy-candidate/boilerplate review queues could all render every
matching row into the DOM at once, with no cap. At the current scale
(hundreds to thousands of rows once filters are broadened) that's slow
to render and hard to scan.

New shared frontend/src/components/Pagination.tsx: a usePagination(items,
resetKey) hook that slices an already-filtered/sorted array client-side
(the data itself is cheap to fetch in one call; DOM row count was the
actual cost), plus a PaginationControls component (page size picker,
prev/next, "X-Y of Z"). resetKey is deliberately keyed to each page's
own filter/search/sort state, not the data array -- DraftListPage polls
every 30s, and resetting to page 1 on every background refresh would
silently kick a reviewer off whatever page they were reading.

Wired into all four pages:
- SkillsTaxonomyPage / JobTitlesTaxonomyPage: straightforward swap of
  the row-map target to pageItems; "select all" bulk actions still
  operate over the full filtered set, not just the current page.
- DraftListPage: same pattern, reset key covers search/type/status.
- ModerationPage's CandidateSection (shared by "Taxonomy candidates"
  and "Boilerplate patterns") gets independent pagination state per
  section, since each already has its own local filter state. Select-
  all stays on the full `visible` list for correctness. The A-Z group
  header logic resets its running letter per page naturally (it's
  recomputed on every render), so a group can repeat its header if it
  spans a page boundary -- accepted as the simplest correct behavior
  rather than adding cross-page bookkeeping for a cosmetic edge case.

Frontend-only change, no backend/API modifications. Verified: npm run
build type-checks and builds clean.
